pages.title: Getting started
pages.summary: Signing in, the menu, Home tasks, favourites, and signing out.
pages.text: Signing in 1. Open the ERP's address in your browser Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox . 2. On Sign In , enter: Corporate ID : your organisation's ID, given by your administrator; Email address and Password : your own ERP account. 3. Select Sign In . You arrive at the menu the Module Hierarchy . If the ERP says your account is inactive or not configured, ask your administrator: an account must be active and assigned to at least one company and role. Forgot your password? On the sign in page, open Forgot Password , enter your email address and select Send Reset Link . A link to set a new password arrives by email. Once signed in, you can change your password at any time from the user menu your name, top right → Change Password . The menu The menu is a tree of areas Finance, Procurement, Inventory and so on . You see only the screens your role allows. Select an area to open it; select a screen to start working in it. Search modules top bar : type part of a screen's name to filter the menu. Enter opens the screen when only one matches; Esc clears the search. The double arrow button expands or collapses the whole tree. Inside a screen, Back to Hierarchy returns to the menu. If you have unsaved changes, the ERP asks before leaving. Favourites Put the screens you use most at the top of the menu: user menu → Configure Favourites , select the star next to each screen you want, then Done . Home tasks The Tasks button top bar shows what is waiting for you, with a count. Select a line to open that document. What you may see, depending on your role: Block What it means Your Pending Approvals Documents waiting for your approval. Rejected — Needs Your Resubmission Your documents an approver rejected, with the reason. Correct and submit again. Ready for You to Act On Approved documents your team follows up for example, raising the purchase order for an approved requisition . The teams are set in Approval Configuration. My Drafts — Not Yet Submitted or Posted Documents you saved as drafts. Post dated Cheques Due to Clear Cheques whose date has come. Recurring Journal Entries Due to Post Recurring entries whose date has come. Company / Employee Documents Expiring Licences, contracts or employee documents near or past expiry. Employee Requests Waiting for You Employees' queries, loan requests and claims to handle. How approvals work is explained in Approvals approvals.html . The user menu Select your name top right for: My Portal : your own leave, payslips and requests, when your ERP user is linked to an employee record; Light mode / Dark mode ; Configure Favourites ; Refresh : reloads the menu after an administrator changed it or your rights ; Change Password ; Log Out . Help The Help button top bar opens this help in a new tab. Inside a screen, it opens that screen's page directly. Signing out, and the automatic sign out Use Log Out in the user menu when you finish, especially on a shared computer. After 10 minutes without activity the ERP warns you, and signs you out 30 seconds later unless you select Stay Signed In . Anything not saved is lost, so save drafts as you go. Next Working with screens working with screens.html : dates, drafts and posting, Copy to Excel, printing, supporting documents, closed months. Approvals approvals.html .

pages.title: Working with screens
pages.summary: What every screen has in common: companies, dates, drafts and posting, messages, Copy to Excel, printing, attachments and closed months.
pages.text: Company first The ERP holds several companies. Most screens start with a Company choice; you see only the companies assigned to you. When you have only one, it is chosen for you. Lists, numbers and reports always belong to the company chosen. Dates and periods Dates show as dd/mm/yyyy 31/12/2026 and months as Sep 2026 , everywhere: on screen, in print and in what you copy to Excel. To enter a date, use the date field's calendar. Drafts, submitting and posting Entry screens journals, invoices, receipts and so on follow the same steps: 1. New opens an empty document. Fill the header company, date, party and the lines. 2. Save Draft keeps your work without any effect on the books or stock. Drafts appear in Home tasks under My Drafts , and you can change or delete them. 3. Submit or Post : where an approval is set up for that document, Submit sends it to the approver see Approvals approvals.html ; otherwise Post records it: the accounting entry and any stock movement are made, and the document gets its number. 4. A posted document cannot be edited. To correct it, Reverse it a mirror entry, dated in an open month and enter it again. The list on each entry screen shows documents by status; search and open any of them. Messages and questions Messages, confirmations "Post this document?" and questions for example a reason for a reversal appear in a box inside the ERP. Read them before choosing: Cancel always leaves things as they were. Copy to Excel and printing Copy on lists and reports copies the table; paste it into Excel and each value lands in its own cell. Print prints the report or document without the menus and buttons. To keep a PDF, choose "Save as PDF" as the printer. Supporting documents Entry screens have a Supporting documents section: Add files to keep the vendor's bill, a delivery note or a receipt with the document. Files are stored in the company's document storage, and anyone who can open the document can open its files. Closed months Finance closes each month after its checks Period Closing . Once a month is closed, nothing can be posted, reversed or approved with a date in it; the ERP says which month is closed. Use a date in an open month, or ask someone with the reopen right to reopen the month. Drilling down and going back Reports link to their detail a Trial Balance line to its ledger, a ledger line to its document . Use Back to … on the opened screen to return to the report where you left it. Saving your place The ERP signs you out after 10 minutes without activity with a warning . Save drafts as you go on long entries.

pages.title: Approvals
pages.summary: How documents are submitted, approved, rejected and delegated.
pages.text: When a document needs approval An administrator decides, per document type and company, whether documents need approval and by whom Approval Configuration . Rules can depend on the amount, and a document can need several approvers one after another. When a rule applies, Submit sends the document for approval instead of posting it. Approving 1. Your pending approvals appear in Home tasks under Your Pending Approvals . 2. Select one to open the document. Check it, and its attachments. 3. Choose Approve , or Reject with a reason. A reason is required to reject. When the last approver approves, the document is posted or, for an order or a request, becomes approved for the next step . Where a follow up team is set in Approval Configuration for example Procurement for approved requisitions , the document appears in that team's Home tasks under Ready for You to Act On . Rejected documents A rejected document returns to its submitter, with the reason, under Rejected — Needs Your Resubmission . Correct it and submit it again. Following a document Approval Tracker shows where every submitted document is: who has approved it, who it is waiting for, and since when. When an approver is away From Approval Tracker, an approver can delegate their own pending approvals, and an administrator can delegate anyone's, to another user who has access to that screen and company. A reason is required for example "On annual leave" ; who delegated, to whom and when is recorded. Closed months An approval that would post into a closed month is refused; see Working with screens working with screens.html closed months .

pages.title: Chart of Accounts
pages.summary: The list of accounts every entry posts to: heads and postable accounts, types, codes, and shared accounts.
pages.text: Chart of Accounts What it is for Every amount the ERP records lands on an account in the Chart of Accounts COA . The COA is a tree: header accounts group others for example "Current Assets" , and postable accounts receive journal lines for example "Bank — Main Account" . Before you start You need the Chart of Accounts right for your role Roles & Permissions . Decide which accounts are for one company and which are shared by all companies for example a common expense list . Step by step Add an account 1. Open Chart of Accounts and select Add Account . 2. Choose the Parent Account the head it sits under . Choose "None" to start a new top level group. 3. Enter the Name and choose the Type : Asset, Liability, Equity, Revenue, Cost of Goods Sold or Operating Expense. The normal balance debit or credit follows from the type. 4. Choose Postable if journal lines may post to it; leave it unticked for a header. 5. Choose the Company , or Shared All Companies . 6. For a header, you can set the Cash Flow Category Operating, Investing, Financing ; the accounts beneath it follow it in the Cash Flow Statement. 7. Select Save Account . The code is given automatically: the next number under the parent. Find accounts Filter by company, type, status, or "Postable only". Choosing a company shows its own accounts and the shared ones; "Shared All Companies " shows only shared ones. Move an account to another head Change its Parent Account and save. The account gets the next code under the new head, only if it has never been used . Once anything has posted to it or a document refers to it , the move is refused: create a new account under the right head, move the balance with a journal entry journal entries.html , and set the old one Inactive. Retire an account Set its Status to Inactive . It stays in the history and reports but can't be used in new entries. Good to know Some accounts are control accounts , kept by their own screens: each vendor's payables and each customer's receivables account in the Vendor and Customer masters , and each item's inventory account. Lines on a party's control account must name the party; see Paying and allocating payments and allocation.html . Cash accounts have codes starting 10 , bank accounts 11 ; Cash and Bank Transactions offers only those as the cash or bank side.

pages.title: Currency Configuration
pages.summary: The currencies list and the default (functional) currency every entry is recorded in.
pages.text: Currency Configuration What it is for Sets the default functional currency the books are kept in. Every journal entry, invoice and report is in that currency; entry screens show it in their read only Currency field. Before you start Only users with Currency Configuration rights normally Admin can change it. Set it once, before the first entry. Step by step 1. Open Currency Configuration and select Add Currency . 2. Enter the Code ISO 4217 , for example AED or USD , the Name and the Symbol . 3. Tick Set as default functional currency for the one the books use. 4. Save. Only one active currency is the default. Good to know The ERP records amounts in the default currency only; there are no exchange rates. Enter foreign currency documents at their value in the default currency. Changing the default later does not convert anything already posted, so choose it before going live.

pages.title: Opening Balances
pages.summary: Bring a company's position on its go-live date into the ERP: the trial balance, opening stock and unpaid invoices.
pages.text: Opening Balances What it is for When a company starts using the ERP, its balances from the old system are brought in once, dated the day before go live go live 1 January → opening date 31 December . Three kinds, each on its own tab: GL : the trial balance every account except the control accounts ; Stock : quantity and unit cost per item and warehouse; Open Invoices : each vendor's and customer's unpaid documents and advances, so statements, aging and payment allocation work from day one. Before you start Opening Balances is for Admin users. An Equity account for Opening Balance Clearing for example "Opening Balance Clearing" . Items, warehouses, vendors and customers already set up Master Data Import helps . Step by step 1. Choose the Company , set the Opening date and the Opening Balance Clearing account , and select Save setup . 2. On a tab, select Copy headers or Copy headers with a sample row , paste into Excel, fill it in, then copy the rows and paste them into the grid. 3. Select Check . Every problem is listed by row and column an unknown account, a missing batch number, a document entered twice… . Fix them in Excel and paste again. 4. When the check is clean, select Post . All rows post together, or none. 5. Repeat for the other tabs. When all three are in, the Clearing balance shown must be zero : then the GL, stock and open invoices agree. What each tab takes Tab Columns required ones marked on the screen GL Account, Debit, Credit, Description, Cost Center, Profit Center Stock Item, Warehouse, Quantity, Unit Cost, Batch No, Expiry Date Open Invoices Party Type, Party, Document Type Invoice / Advance , Document No, Document Date, Due Date, Amount, Description What happens in the books All dated on the opening date: GL : one entry with your rows; the difference goes to Clearing. Stock : the stock comes in at your cost Dr each item's Inventory account, Cr Clearing . Open Invoices : one entry per party on its control account, each document kept with its own number, date and due date, so payments can be allocated against it like any invoice. Inventory, Trade Payables and Trade Receivables are not entered on the GL tab: their balances come from the Stock and Open Invoices tabs. Corrections A posted batch can be Reversed as a whole Admin, any time , then a corrected one posted. A reversal is refused when a document in it has already been paid, or the stock has since been used; undo those first. Good to know Amounts are in the default currency; quantities in the item's base unit. Dates in the paste may be dd/mm/yyyy or yyyy mm dd; at most 2,000 rows. The opening date and clearing account are fixed while any batch is posted.

pages.title: Journal Entries (JV)
pages.summary: Record any accounting entry by debits and credits: accruals, corrections, reclassifications, write-offs.
pages.text: Journal Entry Processing (JV) What it is for A Journal Voucher JV records an entry directly in the accounts: debit and credit lines that must balance. Use it for anything no other screen records: accruals and provisions, corrections, reclassifications, discounts and write offs, settling an advance against a bill. For money in or out of a cash or bank account, use Cash and Bank Transactions cash and bank.html instead. Before you start The accounts exist and are postable see Chart of Accounts chart of accounts.html . Expense, revenue and cost of sales lines need a cost center . Step by step 1. Open Journal Entry Processing JV and select New Journal Entry . 2. Fill the header: Company , Entry Date , Description , and if used the Reference , Division , Branch , Cost Center and Profit Center the header's cost and profit centers are the lines' defaults . 3. Add the lines: Account Code , Debit or Credit , description, and the cost or profit center where needed. You can paste lines from Excel into the grid. 4. A line on a vendor's or customer's account needs the Vendor / Customer , and its Allocate see Paying and allocating payments and allocation.html . 5. Check that total debits equal total credits. 6. Save as Draft to finish later, or Post Entry . Where an approval is set up, the entry goes for approval instead see Approvals approvals.html . Correcting a posted entry A posted entry can't be edited. Select Reverse Entry , choose the reversal date in an open month : a mirror entry is posted and the original stays on record. Then enter the right one. The description of a posted entry can still be corrected with the edit button next to it. Entries posted by other screens invoices, cheques, payroll, opening balances… are reversed from their own screen; the JV screen refuses them and says where. What happens in the books When posted, each line is recorded on its account and date, and the entry gets its numbers: the JV number per company and year and the Txn Ref the finance reference, shared with other finance documents . It shows in the General Ledger general ledger.html , Trial Balance trial balance.html and the statements. Rights Viewing, drafting and posting are separate rights Roles & Permissions . Approval, where set up, is by the approvers in Approval Configuration. Questions and mistakes "…is closed for …" : the entry date is in a closed month. Use a date in an open month, or ask for the month to be reopened Period Closing period closing.html . A cost center is required : expense, revenue and cost of sales lines need one. A party is required : a line on a vendor's payables or customer's receivables account must name that party, and only that party's own account may be used.

pages.title: Cash and Bank Transactions (CBT)
pages.summary: Payments, receipts and transfers through cash and bank accounts, with vendor and customer allocation.
pages.text: Cash and Bank Transactions (CBT) What it is for Records every movement through a cash or bank account: Type Use it for Bank Payment / Cash Payment Paying a vendor, an expense, an advance Bank Receipt / Cash Receipt Money received from a customer or anyone else Fund Transfer Moving money between your own cash and bank accounts Before you start Your cash accounts codes starting 10 and bank accounts codes starting 11 in the Chart of Accounts chart of accounts.html . Vendors and customers set up with their payables / receivables account. Step by step 1. Open Cash and Bank Transactions and select New Transaction . 2. Choose the Transaction Type , then the Company . 3. Choose the Ledger Account : the cash or bank account the money moves through for a Fund Transfer, the account it moves from . 4. Fill the date, description and reference. 5. Add the other side, one line per account: who it was Paid To , Received From , or for a transfer the account it goes To ; the Amount , a description, and a cost center where the account needs one. 6. For a vendor or customer, pick the Vendor / Customer and Allocate the amount to their bills see Paying and allocating payments and allocation.html . 7. Save as Draft , or post. Where an approval applies to that transaction type, it goes for approval instead. 8. Print gives the payment or receipt voucher. Correcting a posted transaction Select Reverse Entry and choose the date: a mirror entry is posted and any bills it settled become unpaid again. Then enter it correctly. What happens in the books Payment: Dr each line's account e.g. the vendor's payables , Cr the cash or bank account. Receipt: Dr the cash or bank account, Cr each line's account e.g. the customer's receivables . Fund Transfer: Dr the account it goes to, Cr the account it comes from. The entry gets a Voucher No. per type and company, and a Txn Ref . Rights As Journal Entries: view, draft and post are separate rights. Approval can be set per transaction type Approval Configuration . Questions and mistakes "…is closed for …" : the date is in a closed month Period Closing period closing.html . The allocation doesn't fit : a bill was paid by someone else in the meantime; the ERP checks again when posting. Open Allocate and choose again. Post dated cheques are not entered here: use Post dated Cheques post dated cheques.html .

pages.title: Paying and allocating against bills
pages.summary: How payments, receipts and adjustments are tied to a vendor or customer and matched to their invoices.
pages.text: Why it matters Each vendor and customer has its own account payables or receivables . To know what is still owed per invoice — for statements, aging and due dates — every amount on those accounts names its party and says what it settles. The two kinds of allocation Kind Meaning Example Against Ref Settles bills or invoices already posted or an earlier advance Paying invoice VI 1021 in full and VI 1034 in part New Ref Opens a new item for the party An advance paid before any bill exists A line's allocations add up to its amount. A line with no allocation chosen is kept as a New Ref for its full amount. Step by step: a payment against bills 1. In Cash and Bank Transactions cash and bank.html Bank Payment , add a line on the vendor's payables account and choose the Vendor / Customer . 2. Select Allocate . The vendor's open items show with their date, due date and Outstanding amount. 3. Enter the amount against each bill, or select Oldest first to fill from the oldest. Clear starts again; Done keeps it. 4. Post. The bills show as Paid or Partly paid in the invoice lists. Settling an advance against a bill Use a Journal Entry journal entries.html with two lines on the vendor's account: one Against the bill, one Against the advance, same amount on opposite sides. Discounts and write offs A JV: the party line Against the invoice, and the discount or write off amount on the expense or income account on the other line. Good to know A party line may only use that party's own payables or receivables account. When posting, the ERP checks again that each bill still has enough outstanding; if someone else paid it meanwhile, the post is refused with the reason. An invoice can't be reversed while payments are allocated to it: reverse those payments first. Due dates are the invoice date plus the party's payment terms.

pages.title: Recurring Journal Entries
pages.summary: Entries that repeat on a schedule — rent, depreciation-like accruals, prepaid expenses spread over months.
pages.text: Recurring Journal Entries What it is for A recurring entry is a template that posts the same journal on a schedule: monthly rent accrual, a prepaid insurance spread over twelve months, a monthly provision. Each run becomes a normal journal entry dated on its run date. Before you start The accounts exist, as for a Journal Entry journal entries.html . Step by step 1. Open Recurring Journal Entries and select New Recurring Entry . 2. Fill the header and lines as on a JV. The description may include {MONTH} , {DATE} or {YEAR} for example "Rent {MONTH}" posts "Rent Oct 2026" . 3. Choose the Amounts : Fixed : the lines' amounts on every run; Spread a total : a total shared equally over the runs; Spread by service period : a total over a service period from, to , each month charged for its days; for example 12,000 for 16 Sep – 15 Sep gives 500, then 1,000 a month, then 500. 4. Choose the Schedule : monthly on a day a day past the month's end runs on its last day , monthly at month end, weekly on a weekday, or monthly on the first … last weekday; every 1, 2, 3… months or weeks 3 = quarterly, 12 = yearly . 5. Choose when it Ends : on an end date, or after a number of runs. 6. Check the preview: every run date with its amount. 7. Save , then activate it with approval, where set up . Posting the runs Runs are posted by a person, not automatically. When a run's date comes, Recurring Journal Entries Due to Post appears in Home tasks. Select Post Due Runs on the list for all, or on one entry . Missed past dates are posted each with its own date. Run by run On an entry's run list: Skip a date no posting that month ; Reverse a posted run a mirror entry; then Post again or Skip ; a run that failed an account made inactive, a closed month… shows the reason; fix it and post again. Changing an active entry Pause , edit, then resume it goes through approval again where set up . End stops it for good. What happens in the books Each run posts a journal entry numbered RJV … dated on its run date, seen in the General Ledger like any JV. Reverse runs from this screen, not from the JV screen. Rights As Journal Entries; activating, pausing, ending, skipping and reversing need the post right.

pages.title: Post-dated Cheques (PDC Received and Issued)
pages.summary: Cheques dated in the future: received from customers or issued to vendors, then cleared, bounced or cancelled.
pages.text: PDC Received PDC Issued What it is for A post dated cheque PDC settles invoices on the day you receive or issue it, but the money only moves on the cheque date. These screens keep the cheque in a clearing account until then. PDC Received : cheques from customers. PDC Issued : cheques you give vendors. Before you start In Company Master , the company's PDC Received Clearing and PDC Issued Clearing accounts. The customer or vendor set up with its receivables / payables account. Step by step Record a cheque 1. Select New PDC . 2. Choose the Company and the customer or vendor. 3. Enter the date received or issued, the Cheque Date , Cheque No. , the amount and a description. Received: type the Drawee Bank the customer's bank . Issued: choose your bank account it is drawn on. 4. Allocate the cheque to the invoices it pays or Oldest first . Anything not allocated stays as an advance. 5. If it replaces a bounced cheque, choose it in Replaces . 6. Save Draft , or Post or submit for approval, where set up . Clear it on its date When the cheque date comes, the cheque appears in Home tasks under Post dated Cheques Due to Clear and in the Due to clear view. Select Clear to Bank with the clearing date not before the cheque date ; for a received cheque, choose the bank account it was deposited into. Several cheques can be cleared together with Clear Selected . If it doesn't go through Bounced : the bank returned it. Enter the date and reason; the invoices it settled are open again. Cancel Cheque : withdrawn before clearing, same effect. Undo Clearing : a clearing entered by mistake goes back to Pending. Bank charges for a bounced cheque are entered separately a JV or CBT . What happens in the books Event PDC Received PDC Issued Post Dr PDC Received Clearing · Cr the customer Dr the vendor · Cr PDC Issued Clearing Clear Dr Bank · Cr PDC Received Clearing Dr PDC Issued Clearing · Cr Bank Bounce / cancel The post entry reversed: the party owes again The same The invoices show "Paid PDC pending " until the cheque clears. Statements of account list pending cheques separately. Rights As Cash and Bank Transactions: view, draft, and post which also covers clear, bounce, cancel and undo . Questions and mistakes Refused as a duplicate : the same cheque number and bank, and party is already recorded and not bounced or cancelled. Can't clear before the cheque date. Can't bounce : an advance the cheque created has since been used against an invoice; undo that first.

pages.title: Statements of Account (Vendor and Customer)
pages.summary: Everything posted with one vendor or customer over a period, the running balance, what is still open, and pending cheques.
pages.text: Vendor Statement of Account (SOA) Customer Statement of Account (SOA) What it is for A statement of account SOA shows one vendor's or customer's history for a period: opening balance, every invoice, payment, receipt, note and adjustment with a running balance, the closing balance, and what is still open by document. Step by step 1. Open Vendor Statement of Account or Customer Statement of Account . 2. Choose the Company and the vendor or customer. 3. Choose From and To , and select Run . 4. Read it: the rows with debit, credit and balance; open items : each unpaid document with its due date, days overdue and outstanding amount, and the aging of what is open; pending PDCs : cheques not yet cleared at the end date; a check against the party's account in the General Ledger. 5. Select a document number to open it Back returns to the statement . 6. Print for the party, or CSV to open it in Excel. Good to know The open items always add up to the closing balance, because every amount on a party's account is allocated see Paying and allocating payments and allocation.html . The print leaves out the internal GL check.

pages.title: Customer and Vendor Aging
pages.summary: How old each party's open balance is, in buckets, with advances and pending cheques shown apart.
pages.text: Customer Aging Vendor Aging What it is for Shows, for every customer or vendor with something open, how much is not yet due and how much is overdue by 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 or more than 90 days — to chase collections or plan payments. Step by step 1. Open Customer Aging or Vendor Aging . 2. Choose the Company and the As at date today by default . 3. Choose Age by : Days overdue from the due date : Not yet due, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, over 90; Days since the invoice date : 0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 91–120, over 120. 4. Select Run . 5. Each row is one party: payment terms, the buckets, Owed , Unapplied credits advances and credits not matched to an invoice , Net balance , and Pending PDCs shown, not deducted . 6. Select a row to see its open documents; SOA opens the party's statement statements of account.html . 7. Copy to Excel or Print . Good to know The report checks its total against the parties' accounts in the General Ledger at that date and says whether they agree. Each party's figures agree with its statement of account at the same date.

pages.title: General Ledger Report (Ledger and Listing)
pages.summary: Every line posted to an account, with its opening, running and closing balance; or a plain listing across several accounts.
pages.text: General Ledger Reports (GL) What it is for The General Ledger shows what was posted to an account and why. It has two views: Ledger : one account over a period, with opening balance, every line, running balance and closing balance; Listing several accounts : the lines of any accounts you pick, by date, without balances, with debit and credit totals. Step by step Ledger 1. Open General Ledger Reports GL , keep Ledger selected. 2. Choose the Company , the Account , From and To . 3. If needed, narrow by Division , Branch , Cost Center or Profit Center . 4. Tick Include Draft entries to see drafts as well marked DRAFT; their figures may still change . 5. Select Run Report . Listing 1. Select Listing several accounts . 2. Pick an account and select Add or press Enter ; repeat for more. A header account brings in every account beneath it. Remove one with its ×. 3. Choose the dates and filters, and run it. From a line to its source Select the Txn Ref to see the whole journal GL Impact : every line with account, cost center, debit and credit. From there, Copy to Excel or Open source document the invoice, payment, cheque… that posted it . Select the Voucher No. to open the source document directly. Copy Table and Print follow the view on screen. Good to know Reports such as the Trial Balance trial balance.html open the General Ledger for an account when you select it; Back returns. A listing shows at most 20,000 lines; narrow the dates or accounts if asked.

pages.title: Trial Balance
pages.summary: Every account's opening balance, movements and closing balance for a period, with drill-down to the ledger.
pages.text: Trial Balance (TB) What it is for The Trial Balance lists every account with its Opening balance, the period's Transactions debit and credit and its Closing balance. Total debits equal total credits; it is the first check that the books are complete. Step by step 1. Open Trial Balance TB . 2. Choose the Company and the period. From starts at the beginning of the company's financial year; change it as needed. 3. Narrow by Division , Branch , Cost Center or Profit Center if needed. 4. Select Run Report . 5. Select an account to open its General Ledger general ledger.html for the same period; Back returns here. 6. Copy Table to Excel, or Print . Before year end closing After a financial year is closed, its income and expense accounts are zeroed into Retained Earnings by the year end closing entry. Tick Before year end closing to see the closed year's income and expense balances as they were. Good to know Anything dated before From is in the Opening column. See Period Closing period closing.html for the year end entry.

pages.title: Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow
pages.summary: The three financial statements, with drill-down from each figure to the ledger.
pages.text: Profit and Loss Statement (P&L) Balance Sheet (BS) Cash Flow Statement (CFS) What it is for Statement Shows Period Profit and Loss P&L Revenue, cost of sales and expenses, and the profit From – To Balance Sheet Assets, liabilities and equity As of a date Cash Flow Statement Cash in and out, by Operating, Investing and Financing From – To Step by step 1. Open the statement and choose the Company . 2. Choose the period From and To or, for the Balance Sheet, the As Of date. 3. Narrow by Division , Branch , Cost Center or Profit Center if needed for example a P&L per cost center . 4. Select Run Report . 5. Select an account line to open its General Ledger general ledger.html ; Back returns. 6. Copy Table to Excel, or Print . Good to know The P&L leaves out the year end closing entry, so a closed year still shows its profit. The Cash Flow is by the direct method: each cash or bank movement is classed by the account on its other side. That account's Cash Flow Category comes from its header in the Chart of Accounts chart of accounts.html ; without one it counts as Operating. The figures follow the posted entries only; drafts are not included.

pages.title: Period Closing (month-end and year-end)
pages.summary: Check and close each month so nothing more can be posted into it, and close the financial year into Retained Earnings.
pages.text: Period Closing What it is for Closing a month locks it: nothing can be posted, reversed or approved with a date in it, so reported figures stay as reported. Closing the year moves its profit or loss into Retained Earnings. Before you start On the Setup tab, per company: the Financial year : January – December or April – March fixed after the first year end ; the Retained Earnings account ; the checklist : each item set to Block the month can't close while it finds something , Warn listed, but the month can still close or Off not checked . Checklist item Drafts dated in the period, not posted Documents waiting for approval Recurring journals due and not posted Depreciation not run for the month Payroll for the month not posted Post dated cheques matured and not cleared Customer Aging agrees with the receivables accounts Vendor Aging agrees with the payables accounts Stock value agrees with the inventory accounts The Trial Balance balances Step by step Close a month 1. Open Period Closing , choose the Company ; the Months grid shows the year. 2. On the first open month, run the Checklist : each item shows what it found, with the documents. 3. Fix what blocks, then select Close . Months close in order. Reopen a month Select Reopen on it and give the reason. The months after it reopen too; the ones before stay closed. Every close and reopen is in the Log . Close the year When all twelve months are closed and the previous year is closed , select Close the year . After you confirm, a Year End Closing entry YEC … dated on the last day of the year moves every income, cost of sales and expense balance, by account and cost center, to Retained Earnings. Reopen the year with a reason reverses that entry; a month of a closed year can't be reopened until its year is. What happens in the books Closing a month posts nothing. Closing the year posts the Year End Closing entry. The P&L financial statements.html leaves it out; the Trial Balance trial balance.html can show the year before it. Payroll and depreciation in a closed month Reversing or redoing a payroll run, a settlement, a loan or depreciation of a closed month offers to date it in the first open month instead; the entry records the original date. Rights Viewing and the checklist: Period Closing access. Closing and reopening are separate rights by default Admin and Finance Manager . Questions and mistakes "yyyy mm is closed for …" on any screen: the document's date is in a closed month. Use an open month's date, or reopen the month here. Can't close : a blocking checklist item found something; open it to see the documents.
